name: Charles Thompson Memorial Hall (St. Paul Deaf Club)
whatItIs: Deaf clubhouse dedicated Nov. 5, 1916, owned by the Deaf community and run by Deaf volunteers; Friday Coffee and ASL, board game nights, bingo, Vikings tailgates, holiday parties and hall rentals.
evidence: Own site lists hours (Fri 10 a.m.-3 p.m., Fri 6-10:30 p.m., Sat 5-10 p.m.), a 2026 rental form and events through Dec. 31, 2026, including the 110th anniversary on Nov. 13-14, 2026.

name: TPleski Woodworking
neighborhoodOrCity: Twin Ports origins; sells at Minnesota craft shows
whatItIs: Wood and epoxy resin trays, boards, boxes and furniture by Deaf woodworker Todd Pleski; listed in MADC's Deaf Business Directory.
evidence: Own site lists 2026 shows on Nov. 21 (Howard Lake) and Nov. 29, 2026. MADC directory lists it as Deaf-owned.

name: Pam's Delicious BBQ
whatItIs: Barbecue business of Pam Burry, listed in MADC's Deaf Business Directory.
evidence: Listed in MADC directory (site copyright 2004-2025); its linked Facebook page could not be opened.

name: ILY by Tricio
whatItIs: Business listed under Patrick Vellia in MADC's Deaf Business Directory. MPR News photographed a DeafBlind baker named Patrick Tricio at the 2024 Deaf Iftar in St. Paul.
evidence: Listed in MADC directory; the linked page (ilybytricio.dbsan.org) returned 404.

name: ASL Interpreting Services (ASLIS)
whatItIs: Sign language interpreting, video remote interpreting, CART captioning and training; says it contracts with 300+ interpreters and has a Deaf Advisory Board. State grantee for Greater Minnesota interpreting and Protactile training.
evidence: Own site describes current services and a DeafBlind training program announcing a March 1-2, 2025 retreat for speaking deafblind people in St. Cloud; contact page lists the Golden Valley address. Ownership not established.

name: Keystone Interpreting Solutions
whatItIs: Interpreting firm that worked with Deaf interpreters Nic Zapko and JP Beldon on the governor's 2020 pandemic briefings.
evidence: WCCO, May 12, 2020 names Zapko working with Keystone. The firm's website did not load, and no 2025 or 2026 dated page was opened.

name: DeafBlind Services Minnesota (DBSM)
type: service provider (LLC of Vision Loss Resources)
whatItIs: Support service providers for DeafBlind adults and interveners for DeafBlind children statewide, funded in part by DHS grants.
evidence: Vision Loss Resources page describes services, links a hiring page and shows the Little Canada office; only a 2026 copyright date, no dated 2025-2026 post.

name: Minnesota Employment Center for People who are Deaf, DeafBlind or Hard of Hearing (MEC)
neighborhoodOrCity: St. Paul (2375 University Ave. W., Suite 160)
whatItIs: Career exploration, job placement, coaching and accommodation support with Deaf and hearing staff fluent in ASL; youth transition services.
evidence: Own site describes services (2026 copyright only); United Way 211 listing gives the St. Paul address. No dated 2025-2026 post was seen.

name: Starkey Hearing Technologies
whatItIs: Hearing technology company; its Starkey Cares program sent 100+ walkers to the 2025 Twin Cities Walk4Hearing. Not Deaf-owned; part of the hearing health economy hard of hearing Minnesotans rely on.
evidence: Press release datelined Eden Prairie, June 26, 2025, describes current operations and its CEO's role as national Walk4Hearing co-chair.

name: HLAA Twin Cities Chapter newsletter
whatItIs: Monthly newsletter and captioned chapter meetings for people with hearing loss.
evidence: Home page links an October 2026 newsletter and a Nov. 21, 2026 meeting.

name: Minnesota Deaf Newsletter (formerly Thompson Hall Newsletter)
whatItIs: Newsletter begun in 1957 at Thompson Hall, renamed in 2002, covering community news, the state academy, sports and MADC.
evidence: MNopedia documents its history; no current issue was found. Thompson Hall now offers a monthly email subscription.

name: ThinkSelf online store
whatItIs: Store run by ThinkSelf, a nonprofit for Deaf, DeafBlind and hard of hearing adult education and victim advocacy; its site was built by a Deaf-owned firm.
evidence: Own site invites visitors to 'shop our store' and lists current hotline hours and programs.
